title: Cold rebuild: lag trend and time to drain
summary: Rebuild GrowthPerSecond and SecondsToDrain from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You wrote **Lag trend and time to drain** in *The signals that matter*. Now write it
again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why this one? "Are we falling behind, and when will we have caught up?" is the first question in every lag incident
and the first line of every status update. You should be able to answer it in your head, and in code.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Lag went from 4 000 to 1 000 records in 30 seconds. What does this print?
explain: The lag shrinks by 100 records per second, so the remaining 1 000 are gone in 10 seconds at the same rates. A negative
growth rate is good news, which is why a lag alert should combine a threshold with "still growing".

steps.title: Rebuild the lag trend cold
prompt: Write the two methods again, from memory.
- `double GrowthPerSecond(List<(long TimeMs, long Lag)> samples)`: lag change per second between the first and the
last sample; 0 with fewer than two samples.
- `double? SecondsToDrain(long lag, double producePerSec, double consumePerSec)`: 0 when there is no lag, `null` when
consumers are not faster than producers, otherwise `lag / (consumePerSec - producePerSec)`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
